newsitem.title: DUBAI: Qatar, Saudi sign border demarcation deal-agency.
newsitem.headline: Qatar, Saudi sign border demarcation deal-agency.

text.p: Saudi Arabia and Qatar have signed a deal with a French company to demarcate their mutual borders in a bid to end a row which had strained relations and led to clashes, the Qatar News Agency (QNA) said on Sunday.

"The Qatar News Agency has learned that a deal was signed yesterday, Saturday, in (the Saudi capital) Riyadh to demarcate the land borders and define the sea borders between the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and Qatar together with the company AGN France International," the official agency said.
The two rich Gulf oil states agreed in April to end the long-standing border dispute, which in 1991 led to clashes in which three people were killed.
Qatar, a pensinsula off the eastern coast of Saudi Arabia, has the world's largest gas reserves while Saudi Arabia is the world's top oil producer and exporter.
